correctness.rationale: Complete coupon-coverage inclusion-exclusion gives the joint CDF factorization on K_(n,n). Conditioning on the first/second distinct coupons proves the exact strict odd difference. Coefficients of constant and first missing-coupon term cancel in the even difference; the unique leading product coefficient is 1, and other exponential bases are at most 1-2/n < (1-1/n)^2. A pathwise coupling dominates collocated starts and excludes a stochastically best random mixture. 1171 exact checker assertions and independent small graph state-DP comparisons passed. Limits: n fixed then time grows; no mean-order or other graph claims.

originality.rationale: The comparison is for full cover-time CDFs, not just expectation or order-of-magnitude speed-up. Accessible primary works give coarser multi-walk results. Actual searches of multi-walker graph coverage, starting-location effects, coupon collector parity, and stochastic dominance found no directly dominating result. The priority assessment is best-knowledge and not a uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: A full historical-priority search of all graph-cover-time distributions is not possible; an earlier result could imply this theorem under a different formulation.
The claim applies only to synchronous non-lazy random walks on K_(n,n); changing the transition or observation protocol changes the parity argument.
No independent mathematical review has been undertaken.

value.rationale: Parallel-walk deployment on symmetric graphs motivates comparing success at every deadline. For every balanced complete bipartite size, the theorem prevents a single deterministic or randomized deployment from optimizing all deadlines, with exact opposite parity tail rates. This is structural stochastic-order information beyond the classical expectation or big-O cover-time analysis; not a mere parameter substitution or isolated finite computation.
